summary: This bill requires colleges applying for federal R&D grants to certify they do not operate branch campuses in China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, or seven other listed countries.

scores.thoughts: The bill imposes an eligibility certification requirement on institutions of higher education seeking federal R&D awards but does not alter appropriation levels, authorize new spending, or cut existing programs. It is a compliance condition rather than a fiscal measure.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.
No provisions address healthcare delivery, insurance, or medical research funding structures.
The legislation has no connection to firearms regulation or Second Amendment issues.
No immigration, visa, or border policy elements are present.
The bill does not address reproductive health services or abortion access.
While research security is mentioned, the bill does not modify Department of Defense budgets or defense-related appropriations.
No environmental regulations, climate programs, or energy policy provisions appear in the text.
The bill does not affect welfare programs, entitlements, or social assistance funding.

The bill places a new certification requirement on higher-education institutions applying for federal R&D awards concerning foreign branch campuses. This is a narrow research-security rule rather than a measure addressing public-school funding, federal involvement in K-12 education, or school-choice policies.
No provisions relate to controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
The legislation contains no criminal-sentencing, policing, or justice-reform measures.
Although the bill restricts certain foreign-country engagements by universities, it does not alter tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export rules.
No deficit-reduction, debt-ceiling, or fiscal-responsibility provisions are included.
The bill does not address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No foreign-assistance funding or programs are modified.
The legislation has no bearing on voting access, election administration, or campaign finance.
No data-privacy, technology-regulation, or surveillance provisions are present.
The bill does not address worker protections, collective bargaining, or union rights.
No provisions concern religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
